title: ngwr registry item
description: One installable unit — a theme preset, a block or a component — that any tool can fetch and any author can host. The rules here are enforced by `pnpm check:registry`; see https://ngwr.dev/guides/registry.

$schema.description: This file, so an editor can complete and validate the item as it is written.

name.description: kebab-case, unique within the registry that hosts it.

type.description: A theme is tokens and nothing else. A block composes several ngwr components into a page or a section. A component is one unit of UI.

title.description: Short human name, shown in a picker.

description.description: One sentence on what it is for.

ngwr.description: Compatible ngwr versions, as a semver range — e.g. ">=11".

dependencies.description: npm packages beyond ngwr and its peers.

registryDependencies.description: Absolute https URLs of other registry items this one composes. Relative is meaningless: the resolving CLI does not know where this item came from.

entryPoints.description: The `ngwr/*` subpaths the item imports from. Checked against the real catalog, so a typo fails rather than installing something that will not compile.

cssVars.description: Token overrides per theme. Keys must be `--wr-*`: a preset that sets arbitrary custom properties is not a theme preset, and consumers install one expecting the library's own token layer to be what changes.

files.description: Source files a CLI writes into the consuming project.

path.description: Path inside the item, for humans.

target.description: Where to write it, RELATIVE to the project root. Absolute paths, drive letters, URL schemes (in any case — `FILE:` is a URL too), padding whitespace, null bytes and any `..` segment are rejected — an item is remote content and this is the field an attacker reaches for first. `pnpm check:registry` runs this pattern and the validator over the same adversarial table, so those shapes cannot start disagreeing again.
